chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from al-'Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both):
Regarding the child, when does he pray? He said: When he understands prayer. I asked: When does he understand prayer and it becomes obligatory upon him? He said: At six years of age.
ai.seo_question: At what age does prayer become obligatory for children in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies that the obligation (*wujub*) of prayer begins at age six, contingent upon the child's intellectual capacity (*'aql*) to comprehend the act. In Shia jurisprudence, this marks the transition from the preparatory phase of teaching (*ta'dib*) to the binding duty, reflecting the principle that religious accountability is tied to cognitive maturity rather than mere chronological age.
